BLOB_SCHEDULE sorting is a specification-level property. In Prysm, blob parameters are configured via config/params and not dynamically scheduled. The implementation uses static configuration (mainnet_config.go:313-321) rather than a sorted schedule lookup.
BLOB_SCHEDULE unique epochs is a specification-level constraint. Prysm uses static configuration with predefined fork epochs, not a dynamic BLOB_SCHEDULE data structure.

process_execution_payload parent_hash assertion involves the Engine API boundary with the Execution Layer. This validation occurs in the EL client, not CL. Prysm trusts the EL to perform this validation via the Engine API.
process_execution_payload prev_randao assertion involves the Engine API boundary. This validation is part of EL block validation, not CL block processing.
process_execution_payload timestamp assertion involves the Engine API boundary. Timestamp validation is performed by the EL client.
process_execution_payload blob commitment count validation via get_blob_parameters is specification-level. Prysm validates blob counts using static configuration parameters (MaxBlobsPerBlock).
verify_and_notify_new_payload involves the Engine API trust boundary (tb-006, tb-007). This is handled by the execution client, not Prysm CL.
compute_fork_digest incorporating blob parameters is a specification-level concern. Prysm computes fork digests using the standard fork version mechanism without dynamic blob parameter incorporation.
Fork digest 4-byte truncation is an internal-only specification property. Prysm follows standard fork digest computation patterns.
Different blob configurations producing different fork digests is a specification-level requirement. This is not directly implemented in Prysm which uses standard fork versioning.

compute_proposer_indices producing SLOTS_PER_EPOCH indices is an internal specification invariant. Prysm implements this via helpers.ComputeProposerIndex but does not expose a compute_proposer_indices function directly.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Fork trigger must fire at epoch boundary only
phase1_findings.code_analysis: The CanUpgradeToFulu function correctly implements the specification: (1) slots.IsEpochStart(slot) checks state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0, (2) slots.ToEpoch(slot) == params.BeaconConfig().FuluForkEpoch checks compute_epoch_at_slot(state.slot) == FULU_FORK_EPOCH. Both conditions must be true (epochStart && fuluEpoch).
phase1_findings.boundary_check: The epoch boundary check is enforced by IsEpochStart which verifies slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the guard condition is correctly implemented using && (logical AND), ensuring both conditions must be true

phase3_findings.rationale: The implementation correctly guards the fork trigger with both epoch boundary check and epoch equality check. The logical AND ensures the fork can only trigger at exactly FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundary.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Fork trigger must fire exactly once at FULU_FORK_EPOCH
phase1_findings.code_analysis: CanUpgradeToFulu returns true only when slot is both at epoch boundary AND equals FULU_FORK_EPOCH. Once upgraded, the state version changes to Fulu, and subsequent calls will not match this condition again because the slot advances.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the condition CanUpgradeToFulu checks exact slot equality, so it can only trigger once per chain at the specific fork epoch boundary slot

phase3_findings.rationale: The exactly-once invariant is maintained because CanUpgradeToFulu only returns true for a single specific slot (the first slot of FULU_FORK_EPOCH). Reorgs may process the same slot multiple times, but the upgrade function produces the same deterministic result.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Fork state transition must be irreversible
phase1_findings.code_analysis: UpgradeToFulu creates a new BeaconStateFulu with fork.current_version set to FuluForkVersion. The state version is immutably part of the BeaconStateFulu type. There is no downgrade path in the codebase.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the state versioning system in Prysm uses type-safe state representations. A Fulu state cannot be converted back to Electra state as they are different Go types.

phase3_findings.rationale: Irreversibility is enforced by Go's type system. BeaconStateFulu and BeaconStateElectra are distinct types. The fork only moves forward; there is no DowngradeFromFulu function.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: fork.current_version cannot be reverted to ELECTRA_FORK_VERSION
phase1_findings.code_analysis: The Fork struct is set once during UpgradeToFulu with CurrentVersion = FuluForkVersion. No code path modifies fork.CurrentVersion after state creation.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the Fork field in BeaconStateFulu is set at construction time and not modified by any state transition function

phase3_findings.rationale: The fork.current_version is immutably set to FuluForkVersion during upgrade. No revert mechanism exists in the state transition logic.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: All Electra BeaconState fields must be preserved except fork and proposer_lookahead
phase1_findings.code_analysis: UpgradeToFulu explicitly copies all Electra state fields: GenesisTime, GenesisValidatorsRoot, Slot, LatestBlockHeader, BlockRoots, StateRoots, HistoricalRoots, Eth1Data, Eth1DataVotes, Eth1DepositIndex, Validators, Balances, RandaoMixes, Slashings, PreviousEpochParticipation, CurrentEpochParticipation, JustificationBits, PreviousJustifiedCheckpoint, CurrentJustifiedCheckpoint, FinalizedCheckpoint, InactivityScores, CurrentSyncCommittee, NextSyncCommittee, LatestExecutionPayloadHeader, NextWithdrawalIndex, NextWithdrawalValidatorIndex, HistoricalSummaries, DepositRequestsStartIndex, DepositBalanceToConsume, ExitBalanceToConsume, EarliestExitEpoch, ConsolidationBalanceToConsume, EarliestConsolidationEpoch, PendingDeposits, PendingPartialWithdrawals, PendingConsolidations. Only Fork and ProposerLookahead are newly computed.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Code review confirms all fields are explicitly copied. The spec test (testing/spectest/shared/fulu/fork/upgrade_to_fulu.go) validates this.

phase3_findings.rationale: All Electra state fields are explicitly copied in UpgradeToFulu. The implementation matches the specification, and spec tests validate correctness.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: post.fork.previous_version must equal pre.fork.current_version
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 109 explicitly sets PreviousVersion to beaconState.Fork().CurrentVersion, preserving the fork version history.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the code directly copies the current version to previous version

phase3_findings.rationale: The implementation correctly sets PreviousVersion from the pre-state's CurrentVersion.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: post.fork.current_version must equal FULU_FORK_VERSION
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 110 explicitly sets CurrentVersion to params.BeaconConfig().FuluForkVersion, using the configuration constant.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the code uses the canonical FuluForkVersion from BeaconConfig

phase3_findings.rationale: The implementation correctly sets CurrentVersion to FuluForkVersion from the beacon config.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: post.fork.epoch must equal current epoch at upgrade
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 111 sets Epoch to time.CurrentEpoch(beaconState), which computes the epoch from the pre-state's slot.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - time.CurrentEpoch correctly derives epoch from state.slot

phase3_findings.rationale: The implementation correctly computes the fork epoch from the current state.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: proposer_lookahead must be correctly initialized from pre-fork state
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 100-103 calls helpers.InitializeProposerLookahead with the pre-fork beaconState and current epoch, deterministically computing the proposer lookahead.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the function uses deterministic inputs (pre-state and epoch)

phase3_findings.rationale: The proposer_lookahead is deterministically initialized from the pre-fork state using the standard helper function.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: All clients must compute identical proposer_lookahead
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Cross-client determinism requires testing with multiple implementations (Lighthouse, Nimbus, Lodestar, Teku). Prysm's implementation follows the spec via helpers.InitializeProposerLookahead.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Cannot be verified without cross-client testing infrastructure

phase3_findings.rationale: Single-client audit cannot verify cross-client determinism. Recommend running consensus spec tests across clients.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Beacon node must correctly store and use proposer_lookahead
phase1_findings.code_analysis: The proposerLookahead is assigned to the Fulu state's ProposerLookahead field at line 169.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the lookahead is directly assigned to the state

phase3_findings.rationale: The proposer_lookahead is correctly stored in the Fulu state and accessible for duty computation.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Only active, non-slashed validators can be proposers
phase1_findings.code_analysis: InitializeProposerLookahead uses the standard proposer selection algorithm which filters for active validators and excludes slashed validators.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the proposer selection algorithm enforces eligibility criteria

phase3_findings.rationale: The proposer lookahead correctly uses the standard proposer selection algorithm which enforces validator eligibility.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: upgrade_to_fulu must not mutate the pre-state
phase1_findings.code_analysis: UpgradeToFulu reads from beaconState but creates a new BeaconStateFulu. All reads use getter methods (CurrentSyncCommittee(), Fork(), etc.) which return copies. The new state is constructed via InitializeFromProtoUnsafeFulu(s) where s is a fresh struct.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the function creates a completely new state struct without modifying the input

phase3_findings.rationale: The function is a pure transformation that reads from pre-state and creates a new post-state without mutation.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: sidecar.index must be < NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 37-39 checks if sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns and returns ErrIndexTooLarge if true. This is a strict less-than comparison using >=.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the >= comparison correctly rejects any index >= numberOfColumns (128 on mainnet)

phase3_findings.rationale: The index validation uses >= comparison, correctly implementing the strict less-than requirement from the spec.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: P2P layer must reject invalid sidecars before forwarding
phase1_findings.code_analysis: The gossip validation pipeline calls ValidFields() which internally calls VerifyDataColumnSidecar. Invalid sidecars are rejected with pubsub.ValidationReject before further processing.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the validation is synchronous and mandatory before any other processing

phase3_findings.rationale: The P2P handler correctly rejects invalid sidecars at the gossip validation layer.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: No array access should occur before index validation
phase1_findings.code_analysis: VerifyDataColumnSidecar validates the index BEFORE any array access. The function only accesses sidecar.Index, sidecar.KzgCommitments (length check), sidecar.Column (length check), and sidecar.KzgProofs (length check). No indexing into arrays using sidecar.Index occurs in this function.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the validation function only performs length checks, not indexed access

phase3_findings.rationale: The validation function does not perform any indexed array access; it only validates lengths and the index value.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Empty kzg_commitments list must be rejected
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Lines 41-44 explicitly check for empty KzgCommitments and return ErrNoKzgCommitments.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the empty check is explicit and returns an error

phase3_findings.rationale: Empty kzg_commitments lists are explicitly rejected with ErrNoKzgCommitments.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: P2P layer must reject empty commitment sidecars
phase1_findings.code_analysis: The ValidFields() check in the gossip pipeline includes VerifyDataColumnSidecar which rejects empty commitments.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - validation occurs before any forwarding

phase3_findings.rationale: The P2P validation layer correctly rejects sidecars with empty commitments.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: KZG verification must handle empty inputs gracefully
phase1_findings.code_analysis: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs would receive an empty sidecars slice if all sidecars were filtered out. The function computes count=0 for empty input and would call VerifyCellKZGProofBatch with empty slices, which should handle this edge case.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Edge case is pre-filtered by VerifyDataColumnSidecar before reaching KZG verification

phase3_findings.rationale: Empty commitment sidecars are rejected by VerifyDataColumnSidecar before reaching KZG verification.

audit_items.skip_reason: The epoch-dependent max_blobs_per_block limit (get_blob_parameters) is a specification-level construct. Prysm uses static configuration (MaxBlobsPerBlock from params) rather than dynamic epoch-based lookup. The validation of commitment count against max is performed at block validation time using the static config.
Epoch computation from sidecar.slot for blob limits is specification-level. Prysm validates blobs using static configuration, not epoch-based dynamic limits.
Oversized KZG commitment rejection via get_blob_parameters is specification-level. Prysm uses static MaxBlobsPerBlock config.
Epoch-dependent blob parameter limits during block validation is specification-level. Prysm uses static configuration.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: column, kzg_commitments, and kzg_proofs arrays must have equal length
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Lines 46-49 check that len(Column) == len(KzgCommitments) == len(KzgProofs), returning ErrMismatchLength on mismatch.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the equality check covers all three arrays

phase3_findings.rationale: Array length equality is enforced with explicit checks before any indexed access.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: P2P layer must prevent propagation of mismatched array sidecars
phase1_findings.code_analysis: ValidFields() calls VerifyDataColumnSidecar which enforces array length equality. Invalid sidecars are rejected.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - validation occurs before forwarding decisions

phase3_findings.rationale: The P2P validation layer correctly rejects sidecars with inconsistent array lengths.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: KZG batch verification must not access out-of-bounds
phase1_findings.code_analysis: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs iterates with 'for i := range sidecar.Column' and accesses KzgCommitments[i] and KzgProofs[i]. Since VerifyDataColumnSidecar ensures equal lengths, i is always valid for all arrays.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - length validation is mandatory before KZG verification

phase3_findings.rationale: Array access in KZG verification is safe because length equality is enforced by prior validation.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: cell_indices must all equal sidecar.Index for each sidecar
phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 72 appends sidecar.Index for every cell in the inner loop. This means all cells within a single sidecar share the same index, which is the correct construction.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - the code correctly uses sidecar.Index for all cells of that sidecar

phase3_findings.rationale: Cell indices are correctly constructed using sidecar.Index for all cells within each sidecar.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: P2P peers cannot exploit cell_indices construction
phase1_findings.code_analysis: The sidecar.Index used for cell_indices comes from the sidecar message. It is validated to be < NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS before use. The index cannot be manipulated after validation.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - index is validated and then used directly in verification

phase3_findings.rationale: The sidecar.Index is validated before being used for cell_indices construction.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Beacon node must reject sidecars with mismatched cell content
phase1_findings.code_analysis: KZG verification (verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs) cryptographically binds cells to commitments and column index. If verification passes, the cells are authentic for that column.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - KZG proof verification ensures cells match the claimed column index

phase3_findings.rationale: KZG verification cryptographically ensures cell authenticity for the specified column index.

phase1_findings.property_assertion: Array lengths must be validated before verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch
phase1_findings.code_analysis: VerifyDataColumnSidecar validates len(Column) == len(KzgCommitments) == len(KzgProofs) before any KZG verification occurs.

phase2_findings.exploit_feasibility: Not feasible - validation is mandatory and synchronous

phase3_findings.rationale: Array length equality is validated before invoking KZG batch verification.
